questions.q: Corvell's single shared FIFO queue treats every Case the same regardless of skill needed. What does Omni-Channel skill-based routing change?
options: It deletes the Case queue entirely so no routing is needed
It assigns work directly to agents who hold the required skills, availability, and capacity, instead of strict arrival order
It only works for chat, not phone or email
It guarantees every case is resolved on first contact
questions.explain: Skill-based routing sends work directly to agents who meet the work item's skill requirements, factoring in availability and capacity, rather than handing cases out in plain arrival order the way a basic queue does.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat entitlements/milestones and Omni-Channel routing as two separate architectural layers?
options: Because milestones replace the need for any routing configuration
Because they are mutually exclusive and an org can only use one
Because entitlements answer what a customer is owed and by when, while routing answers who should work the case — different questions, configured separately
Because entitlements only apply to Leads, not Cases
questions.explain: Routing decides assignment (who works the case); entitlements and milestones decide obligation and timing (what the customer is owed and by when). Conflating the two, as Corvell originally did by tracking warranty deadlines as a manually-watched custom field, is what broke down as volume grew.

questions.q: In Salesforce's entitlement model, what is the typical relationship between entitlements and milestones?
options: An entitlement process can only have one milestone, ever
Entitlements require milestones, and neither can exist independently
Milestones are a feature of Omni-Channel, unrelated to entitlements
Milestones require an entitlement process, though an entitlement can exist without milestones
questions.explain: An entitlement can be used on its own to define support eligibility, but milestones (like first response and resolution targets) are tracked within an entitlement process — milestones depend on that process existing, not the other way around.

questions.q: Besides routing efficiency, what other lever does designing a Knowledge base into Corvell's redesign create?
options: It can resolve a customer's question through self-service before a Case is even created, reducing total case volume
It eliminates the need for entitlements entirely
It automatically assigns skills to every agent
It replaces the Omni-Channel routing engine
questions.explain: A well-indexed, customer-facing Knowledge base can answer a question before a Case ever gets created, which reduces how much volume the routing and agents have to handle at all — a bigger lever than making existing case-handling faster.

questions.q: Per Trailhead's stated best practice, what's the risk of attaching too many skill requirements to a single work item under skill-based routing?
options: The case automatically closes without being worked
No agent may hold that exact narrow combination of skills, leaving the work item unroutable
It forces the case back into first-in-first-out queue routing
It disables Entitlements for that Case
questions.explain: Trailhead specifically warns against over-narrow skill combinations: if the combination is too specific, no single agent may ever qualify for that work item, and the risk grows the more skills are stacked onto one requirement.
